Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the TechForward Solutions Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Anya Sharma, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Anya Sharma, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TechForward Solutions’ Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are David Chen, CEO; Sarah Miller, CFO; Michael Davis, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to David.

David Chen, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Anya. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, our Q3 2024 revenue reached $1.739 billion, landing at the upper end of our guidance range of $1.68 billion to $1.74 billion. This reflects strong execution and resilient demand in key segments, despite a challenging macroeconomic environment. While we are pleased with our ability to achieve the high end of guidance, a deeper dive into the underlying factors driving this performance is warranted.

We also continued to drive improvements through our utilization rate, which reached 74.8% this quarter. This contributed significantly to our overall Q3 financial performance, which saw a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. The increase is directly attributable to an enhanced utilization rate and improved pricing strategies across our core service offerings.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our success in securing government-backed initiatives, particularly the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Tax Credit (ITC). We secured $16 million in ITC benefits this quarter, and anticipate these benefits to be a recurring feature throughout the program's duration. This, coupled with strategic local grants and favorable loan terms, positions us favorably for continued growth and innovation. Furthermore, a diligent focus on optimizing our tax strategy resulted in a substantial tax refund for this quarter.

Now I’ll hand it over to Sarah to discuss the financials in greater detail.

Sarah Miller, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, David, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our Non-IFRS gross margin for Q3 2024 landed at 24.7%, a figure we are extremely pleased with. This represents a strong performance exceeding the mid-point of our previously issued guidance range of 23.5% - 24.5%. This has contributed meaningfully to our bottom line, allowing us to reinvest in strategic growth initiatives.

Second, we saw positive contribution from our net margin and diluted EPS. Diluted earnings per share (EPS) reached $0.41, surpassing the high end of our projected range of $0.35-$0.40. This performance was fueled by a combination of robust revenue growth, improved cost management leading to enhanced net margin, and the positive impact of several strategic initiatives implemented over the past year. This resulted in a 20% increase compared to the $0.34 reported in Q3 of the previous year.

And although still early, our CapEx for Q3 was $162 million or roughly 9% of revenue. This level of investment reflects our continued commitment to strategic growth initiatives, technological advancements, and maintaining the operational efficiency of our existing infrastructure.

With that, I’ll turn it to Michael for a deeper look at operational performance.

Michael Davis, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was our Q3 2024 revenue performance, which David touched on earlier. Specifically, sequential revenue increased by 7%, from $1.625 billion in Q2 2024 to $1.739 billion in Q3 2024, particularly in our Cloud Infrastructure division, which experienced a robust 12% QoQ increase in revenue, driven by a combination of increased adoption of our new "ApexScale" platform and expanded contracts with existing enterprise clients.

Additionally, our utilization rate of 74.8% has enabled more efficient project execution and resource allocation. We experienced a noticeable surge in demand for our consulting services, particularly within the technology and healthcare sectors. Several large-scale digital transformation projects, delayed from earlier in the year due to economic uncertainty, were finally greenlit and initiated in Q3. This accounted for roughly 40% of the utilization increase.

We’re also seeing early traction in our Advanced Manufacturing Investment Tax Credit (ITC), where updated processes and investments in our Ohio facility are yielding significant returns. As I mentioned, we received a $16 million credit this quarter, contributing to a sequential decrease in operating expenses. The support from the local governments in the Ohio region has given the business increased capital to grow their footprint in the region, which we believe will lead to a 15% increase in revenue growth in the long term.

Now I’ll pass it to Emily for the tech and product update.

Emily Carter, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Michael.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to our utilization rate improvements, supporting broader adoption and efficiency gains across our project portfolio. Our internal initiatives focused on optimizing resource allocation and skill matching proved highly effective. We implemented a new AI-powered workforce management system in Q2. We saw a 20% reduction in idle time, and a 10% increase in project delivery efficiency during Q3.

We’ve also supported our gross margin improvements, and our investments in automation technologies within our manufacturing facilities are now yielding substantial returns. The implementation of advanced robotics and AI-powered quality control systems has reduced labor costs by 8% YoY and improved production efficiency by 10%. The business is investing heavily in quality control systems, which will decrease the amount of capital needed to fix defective products and thus increase revenue.

And finally, on our Advanced Manufacturing Investment Tax Credit (ITC), our new architecture is enabling us to leverage government incentives and drive innovation. We invested $45 million in robotic assembly lines, qualifying us for a significant portion of the ITC. The credit covers approximately 35% of our eligible capital expenditures in this area. The integration of advanced 3D printing for rapid prototyping and custom component manufacturing, a $15 million investment, further boosted our eligibility for the ITC.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the government grants and tax incentives and whether you anticipate these to continue into the next fiscal year?

David Chen:
Certainly. We are actively leveraging local grant programs to support our operations and expansion. For example, we received a $3 million grant from the state of Ohio based on our commitment to creating over 200 new high-skilled jobs at our Ohio facility. We also secured a $1.5 million grant for our R&D facility in California focused on developing sustainable battery technologies. We expect to continue pursuing these opportunities and anticipate similar benefits in the coming year, but the exact amounts will depend on specific project approvals and policy changes. We have a dedicated team monitoring these opportunities and ensuring we meet all eligibility requirements.

Analyst 2:
On the capital expenditures, how much of that is allocated to the expansion of your data centers, and what is the expected ROI on those investments?

Sarah Miller:
Of the $162 million in CapEx, $35 million was allocated to the expansion of our primary data center in Phoenix, Arizona. This expansion was critical to accommodate the 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year. The new facility incorporates advanced cooling systems, improving energy efficiency by an estimated 18% compared to our older facilities. We anticipate an ROI of approximately 20% within the first three years, driven by increased capacity, improved efficiency, and reduced operating costs.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to the gross margin improvement initiatives?

Emily Carter:
Yes, of course. Our investments in automation technologies within our manufacturing facilities are now yielding substantial returns. The implementation of advanced robotics and AI-powered quality control systems has reduced labor costs by 8% YoY and improved production efficiency by 10%. This is particularly evident in our North American facilities, where we've deployed the "Precision Manufacturing" platform. We also saw approximately $8 million in cost savings related to improved supply chain management and reduced waste in our manufacturing processes.

Analyst 4:
And finally, on the utilization rate, is this sustainable, and what strategies are you implementing to maintain or improve it going forward?

Michael Davis:
We are cautiously optimistic about maintaining strong utilization levels. For Q4, we are providing utilization rate guidance in the range of 73% to 76%. This acknowledges the typical seasonal slowdown we often see during the holiday season, but also reflects our confidence in a continued strong pipeline of projects. We are continuing to invest in our workforce management system and refining our resource allocation processes. We also are exploring the potential of implementing a dynamic pricing model that will further enhance utilization rates.

Closing

David Chen:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
